original: Currently, we lack information.

We should consider the possibility
that it doesn't have a mind.

In which case, we'll probably
have to use brute force.
Can you do it?
I don't know.
In that case,
I may be able to kill Ms. Frieren.
Oh?
Yes.
Well, then...
Let's come up with a strategy.
You're there like the wind
Closing your eyes at sunset
I wonder what's on your mind
With your eyelids open
Your eyes shone like glass
It faintly smelled like a sunny day
Clear up the sky, let flowers bloom
Bloom and blame it on the sunny sky
Even the rain, when it stops
Will make you shine in the sunlight
Calm the stirring sounds in my heart
We go like the sunny wind
Go on and fly over that cloud
Further and further away
To confirm: if the replica has a mind,

we'll use Edel's hypnosis magic
to penetrate my mental defenses,
and Fern will kill me.
Yes.
"Yes"?
Mr. Dünste.
Where is Ms. Edel?

She dropped out when we were
attacked by Sense's replica.
I see. Mr. Blei as well?
I was able to escape because he kept it busy.
I hope he made it out safely.
Leave me! Go!
B-But...
It's better than neither of us passing.
I have information.
Why don't we work together?
That was my intention from the start.
Is there anyone who can treat this man?

I have a holy scripture.
I can cast simple healing spells.
Please.
I see.
The replicas don't have minds.
No. According to Ms. Edel,

they merely imitate the
functions of a mind precisely
without actually having one.

Well, there goes the easy way
of taking one down.
We'll have to plan accordingly.

But, Frieren, there's still
too much that we don't know.

The biggest question is: what are those
replicas, and who created them?

We can hardly take them on
without knowing their nature.

In particular, we need to know whether
or not the replicas themselves
have any unique weaknesses.

If that replica really is as strong as you,
then we'd likely suffer casualties.
I won't answer that question.
Didn't think you would.
They don't have any weaknesses.
The replicas are being controlled

by a monster from the mythical era
known as the Spiegel.
Lawine.
How do you know that?

My oldest brother was in the advance party
that the Continental Magic Association
sent into the Tomb of the Ruined King.

So you had information.
No wonder you made it this far.
But you made an irrational choice.

You should've shared your information
and worked with us from the start.
It didn't feel like we could've at the time.
And Frieren and Fern left before we knew it.
Besides, old man,

you're the type to mercilessly abandon
your allies unless there are rules against it.

Anyone would think twice
about working with you.
She really doesn't like you.
It's true that I'm old,

but there's something that stings
about having it said to my face.
Maybe you should apologize.
Sorry, old man.

According to the advance party's
observation report,

the Spiegel is in the treasure room
on the other side of that door.

The monster itself is weak
and has no way of attacking directly.

Once we defeat it,
all the replicas will disappear.
That matches what our mana detection revealed.
The monster is on the other side of the door,

but it's shut fast with a
powerful sealing spell.

I've confirmed that as well.
My replica must've done it.

It's a spell that shuts the door of a
treasure vault at the risk of your life.

Even among folk magic,
it's a top-class sealing spell.

That door won't open
until the caster is dead.

We could ignore the door
and break through a wall,

but they've probably already
accounted for that.

Either way, we'll have to defeat that replica
if we want to take down the Spiegel.

If we want to take it down,
then we'd better hurry.
What do you mean?

The Spiegel creates replicas
of everyone within the dungeon.

Over time, the replicas begin to gather
at the bottom of the dungeon.

Aside from my brother's unit, most members
of the advance party died...
right here, just before the bottom.
I see.
Excuse me.

The replicas precisely imitate the
functions of a mind, don't they?

In that case, any vulnerabilities
in their behavioral patterns
would be the same as the original's, right?
Probably.
In that case, we may have a chance.
What vulnerability are you thinking of?
Ms. Frieren, could you go stand by that wall?
Okay.
Was that…?
Incredible. I don't believe it.
Did you notice?
Did you?
Nope.
This is Frieren's fatal vulnerability.
Why didn't I notice when I fought her?

No, I couldn't notice because of my
preconceptions about experienced mages.

When casting a spell, she stops
detecting mana for a brief moment.

Isn't that a common mistake
made by apprentice mages?
I've never been very good about it.

If you're aware of it,
then why didn't you say anything?
Because it's embarrassing.
This is hardly the time to be saying that.
But she's far too skilled in all other areas.

I can't imagine there are many mages
who could exploit that vulnerability.
In any case, let's discuss our strategy.

Supposing we can handle Frieren's replica,
what about the others?

Won't they all disappear
if we defeat the Spiegel?
Ms. Frieren, you seem to be having fun.

The replicas will probably
gather before then.
Yeah.
Sounds like we've got a plan.

Eisen will draw the enemy to him,
and I'll attack from the flank.
Frieren, you'll provide supporting fire.
What about Heiter?
Today's an off day for him. He's hungover.
He's dead.

I was just thinking about
all the times we discussed
how we'd beat the dungeon boss like this.
Okay.
Let's begin the attack.
Can we win?

Don't worry. There isn't a dungeon
that can't be conquered.

I'm the mage of the party that cleared
the most dungeons in history.

Are you two sure you don't need any help
fighting Frieren's replica?

The fewer of us there are, the easier
it will be to predict its movements.

We'd almost certainly win if we all fought,
but most of us would probably die.

I doubt we'd even have the time
to use our escape golems.

So slowing down the replicas gathering
at the bottom is more important.
If they surround us, we're all dead.
Follow the plan.
Got it. Good luck.
Open the door.
Now, then.
Let's discuss our weakest matchups.
Judradjim.
It's behaving just like Ms. Frieren predicted.
Vollzanbel.
I stopped detecting mana.
I'll be wary of Fern, who used that opportunity to hide.
But I'll be busy dealing with the equally-matched opponent in front of me.
I won't have time to look for Fern.
After all, no one knows better than I do how frightening I can be.
You'll be all right.

Not even I can easily detect you
when you're completely hidden.

Are you sure I should use
Zoltraak to attack, though?
It's the quickest spell there is.

Besides, Zoltraak is a relatively
new spell for elves.

Not enough time has passed for us
to reflexively defend against it.

It takes only a moment
for us to respond to it,

but the time we spend thinking
about it causes a delay.
You're different, though.

Zoltraak has existed since your birth.
To you, it's nothing special.

It's a fundamental mage spell
engraved into your being.
Your Zoltraak can kill me.
Hit it with all the mana you've got.
Frieren, I thought you didn't like me.
Why have you come to see me?
Honestly, I thought we'd never meet again.
I came to deliver my master's will.
It's been fifty years.
I see. So Flamme has died.
You're not sad?
I only trained her on a whim.
It's practically a report.
What does it say?

The emperor has authorized
magical research nationwide.

Until now, human societies have considered
magic to be a technique used by demons,
and openly studying it was forbidden.
Flamme encouraged him to allow it

and had been training the newly
established imperial mages.
She wants me to take over for her.
Such greed.

Receiving authorization to study magic
is a feat on its own, but she wants more.
Is that such an impressive achievement?

The continent's largest united empire
is set to begin studying magic
and adopting it for military use.
The neighboring nations are sure to respond.

In just a few decades, magic will
spread throughout the continent.

We'll enter an era in which
all of humanity can use magic.
In the near future,

humanity will acquire the strength to fight
back against the Demon King's forces.
I see. That's incredible.
Indeed it is.
But that's not what I want.
Leave, Frieren.
I can't comply with this final request.
I find it truly displeasing.
An era in which anyone can use magic?
Magic should be special.
I won't teach anyone who lacks talent.
How dare she send this to me?

Flamme and I remained unable to understand
each other until the very end.

She was only ever a student
I trained on a whim.

My master said you'd probably
get upset and tear up her will.

But she wanted to tell you her dream
had come true regardless.
It doesn't make sense, does it?
Well, I'm leaving now.
I doubt we'll meet again.
Frieren.
Before you go, walk with me a little.
After all, we have all the time in the world.

An era in which anyone could use magic
was Flamme's dream.
I doubt she cared about helping humanity

or the strength to fight the
Demon King's forces at first.
Do you know what her favorite spell was?
A spell to create a field of flowers.
A useless, foolish spell.
She truly loved magic.

She genuinely wished for everyone in the
world to be able to cast spells like that.
It disgusted me.

It was the fanciful dream of a girl,
but it's what she really wanted.

She told me about this dream of hers
when she was a child much shorter than me.

Honestly, I thought that era
wouldn't arrive for many more years.
I didn't think she could accomplish it.

To me, her life was so short
as to be practically nothing,

and yet she became the founder
of humanity's magic.
My master was always quick to decide.
It felt like she was in a hurry.
Humans have limited lifespans.
They exist much closer to death than we do.

We must all make important decisions
at several points in our lives,
but humans cannot afford to delay them.
We can afford to wait a century or two.

Even ignoring them for a millennium
poses no obstacle,
as our time is closer to an eternity.

Frieren, many years have passed
since humanity created
what could be called a civilization.

From now on, their progress
will begin to accelerate.
A mere thousand years.

In a mere thousand years,
the era of humans will arrive.
The humans will overtake us.
Do not neglect your training, Frieren.

If anyone kills you,
it will be either the Demon King…
or a human mage.
I'm looking forward to it, Serie.

We're going to see so many
different kinds of mages and spells.
And I'm alright
Yeah, I hear you
The wind teases this hair that's longer now
There's meaning in everything
Even the days that came to a halt
Now that I finally understand, I've caught up to you
See, things that couldn't have been
Seen if it weren't for these eyes
Why? They begin to overflow
I won't ask to see you, so at least
Let me remember the past, just for today
So, if we were to meet again
No more hesitations, I'd choose the present
Anytime, anywhere, yah
Anytime, anywhere
I'll be there (close your eyes, and I'll always be there)
Even if there are no absolutes
I'm always aware of your thoughts
Those tears will be alright, dawn will surely break
I'm whispering our lullaby for you to come back home
Now, let's end this.
Worst case, we could both die.
Incredible, Ms. Frieren.
It's up to you.
This opening won't do.
We expected this much.
I'll have to do it after all.
So this is the height of magic.
